about: Domain-neutral principles, reasoning modules and thought frameworks. Per task the model selects 2-4 and adapts them into a reasoning frame (Self-Discover style). Never tune entries to a test task.

entries.name: Known vs inferred
entries.when: any factual claim or diagnosis
entries.form: Separate what you observed, what you inferred, and what you assumed — and say which is which.

entries.name: Seek disconfirmation
entries.when: you have a favoured answer or explanation
entries.form: Before settling, look for the evidence that would prove you wrong.

entries.name: Base rates first
entries.when: judging likelihood, diagnosing, predicting
entries.form: Start from how often this is true in general, then adjust for the specifics.

entries.name: Prefer reversible moves
entries.when: acting under uncertainty; deleting, sending, buying, overwriting
entries.form: Prefer actions that can be undone; slow down and confirm before irreversible ones.

entries.name: Chesterton's fence
entries.when: removing, replacing or 'cleaning up' something that exists
entries.form: Find out why something is there before changing or removing it.

entries.name: Steelman
entries.when: comparing positions, options or arguments
entries.form: State the strongest version of the other option or view before judging it.

entries.name: Resolve ambiguity
entries.when: the request has more than one reasonable reading with different outcomes
entries.form: Ask when readings lead to different actions with real cost; otherwise state the reading you chose.

entries.name: Serve the purpose
entries.when: every request
entries.form: Find the goal behind the literal request and serve it — without going beyond what was asked.

entries.name: Proportionality
entries.when: deciding how much effort, checking or caution to apply
entries.form: Match effort, verification and caution to the stakes.

entries.name: Second-order effects
entries.when: decisions, policies, changes to systems
entries.form: Ask 'and then what?' — consequences of consequences, including for others.

entries.name: Opportunity cost
entries.when: choosing between options or spending time/money
entries.form: Compare against the best alternative, not against doing nothing.

entries.name: Simplest sufficient
entries.when: explaining, designing, fixing
entries.form: Prefer the simplest explanation or solution that fully fits; add complexity only when evidence demands it.

entries.name: Calibration
entries.when: stating conclusions
entries.form: Match confidence to evidence; give likelihoods or ranges when uncertain; 'I don't know' is a valid answer.

entries.name: Map is not territory
entries.when: relying on summaries, labels, docs, memory or models of a system
entries.form: Check against the actual source, file or system, not a description of it.

entries.name: Incentives
entries.when: weighing sources, claims, advice, behaviour
entries.form: Ask who benefits; sources and people respond to incentives.

entries.name: Inversion
entries.when: planning to achieve a goal
entries.form: Ask what would guarantee failure, and avoid it.

entries.name: Local vs global
entries.when: optimising one part of a system, code, plan or process
entries.form: An improvement in one part can harm the whole; check the system-level effect.

entries.name: Time horizon
entries.when: trade-offs between now and later
entries.form: Weigh short-term against long-term; the best move now may not be best later.

entries.name: Ignore sunk costs
entries.when: deciding whether to continue an approach that is struggling
entries.form: Past effort doesn't justify continuing; decide on what lies ahead.

entries.name: Most informative next step
entries.when: uncertain about which step to take next
entries.form: Prefer the next step whose result would most change your mind.

entries.name: Respect stated constraints
entries.when: the user gave preferences, limits or rules
entries.form: Honour stated constraints and preferences; don't override them for elegance or speed.

entries.name: Name the trade-off
entries.when: options compete on different values
entries.form: Make the trade-off explicit rather than hiding it inside a recommendation.

entries.name: Robustness
entries.when: the future is uncertain
entries.form: Prefer choices that work across many plausible futures over one that is optimal in only one.

entries.name: Specifics expose errors
entries.when: an argument or plan feels convincing but abstract
entries.form: Test it with concrete examples, numbers and cases; abstractions hide mistakes.

entries.name: Define terms
entries.when: a key word is vague, technical or disputed
entries.form: Pin down what the key terms mean before reasoning with them.

entries.name: Reference class
entries.when: the situation is unfamiliar or novel
entries.form: Borrow from similar cases — what usually happens with things like this — and expect surprises.

entries.name: Care for people
entries.when: actions or advice affect people
entries.form: Weigh effects on people; keep honesty and consent; don't trade them for convenience.

entries.name: Close the loop
entries.when: finishing any task
entries.form: A task is done only when the result is checked against the original goal.

entries.name: Restate
entries.when: start of any non-trivial task
entries.form: Restate the problem in your own words; list givens, unknowns and constraints.

entries.name: Decompose
entries.when: the task has several parts or is too big to hold at once
entries.form: Break it into parts that can be solved separately; solve; recombine and check the joins.

entries.name: Surface assumptions
entries.when: the answer depends on things not stated
entries.form: List your assumptions; mark the ones that, if wrong, would change the answer; check those.

entries.name: Generate alternatives
entries.when: choosing an approach, design or answer
entries.form: Produce 2-4 genuinely different options before choosing one.

entries.name: Work backwards
entries.when: the end state is clear but the path isn't
entries.form: Start from the desired result and derive the steps that lead to it.

entries.name: Analogy
entries.when: a similar problem has a known solution
entries.form: Find the similar solved problem; map what transfers and note what doesn't.

entries.name: First principles
entries.when: convention or habit may be misleading
entries.form: Reduce to what is fundamentally required and rebuild from there.

entries.name: Critical check
entries.when: after drafting reasoning or an answer
entries.form: Look for flaws, gaps and contradictions as a demanding expert would.

entries.name: Edge cases
entries.when: rules, code, plans, generalisations
entries.form: Test on extreme, empty, unusual or adversarial cases.

entries.name: Perspectives
entries.when: decisions affecting several parties; persuasive or sensitive writing
entries.form: View it from each stakeholder: the user, others affected, an expert, a skeptic.

entries.name: Root cause
entries.when: something failed or keeps failing
entries.form: Ask why repeatedly until reaching a cause you can act on.

entries.name: Constraints first
entries.when: many options, some disallowed
entries.form: Identify hard constraints and eliminate options that violate them before comparing the rest.

entries.name: Quantify
entries.when: magnitudes, costs or probabilities matter
entries.form: Use numbers you were given or can source, and compute rather than guess; without data, compare in relative terms and name what to measure — never invent figures.

entries.name: Timeline
entries.when: events, histories, processes, dependencies
entries.form: Lay events or steps out in time order and check what depends on what.

entries.name: Risk scan
entries.when: before acting on anything that matters
entries.form: What could go wrong? Likelihood times impact; add mitigations for the top risks.

entries.name: Simplify first
entries.when: the full problem is hard to attack
entries.form: Solve a smaller or simpler version first, then generalise.

entries.name: Categorize
entries.when: meeting an unfamiliar thing, term or problem
entries.form: Ask what kind of thing or problem this is, and what is typical for that kind.

entries.name: Weigh evidence
entries.when: sources disagree or vary in quality
entries.form: Rate each piece by source quality, directness and agreement; prefer primary over secondary.

entries.name: Check every condition
entries.when: questions or tasks with several qualifiers (dates, roles, scopes, exceptions)
entries.form: List every condition in the request and confirm the answer satisfies each one.

entries.name: Competing hypotheses
entries.when: explaining an observation or diagnosing
entries.form: Hold several explanations; find the observation that distinguishes them.

entries.name: Find the bottleneck
entries.when: improving speed, throughput or outcomes
entries.form: Find the step that limits the whole and improve that first.

entries.name: Reframe
entries.when: stuck, or the obvious framing may bias the answer
entries.form: Change the framing (gain vs loss, cost vs benefit, whose problem it is) and see what shifts.

entries.name: Map uncertainty
entries.when: incomplete information
entries.form: Mark what is certain, likely and unknown; plan to reduce the unknowns that matter most.

entries.name: Keep options open
entries.when: early in uncertain work
entries.form: Prefer steps that keep options open or buy information cheaply.

entries.name: Counterfactual
entries.when: judging whether an action helps
entries.form: What happens if we do nothing, or the opposite?

entries.name: Abstraction ladder
entries.when: the problem is stated at the wrong level
entries.form: Move up (why? which principle?) and down (how? which concrete step?) to find the right level.

entries.name: Verify externally
entries.when: key claims, numbers or code
entries.form: Check against a source, run it, or test it — don't trust your own recall.

entries.name: Conversational intent
entries.when: chat, advice, emotionally loaded or vague messages
entries.form: Identify what the person needs (information, a decision, reassurance, an action) and their unspoken question.

entries.name: Decision matrix
entries.when: choosing among several options on several criteria
entries.form: 1) options 2) criteria that matter to this person 3) compare each option on them (qualitatively unless you have real data) 4) sanity-check the winner against intuition and reversibility 5) recommend, naming the trade-off.
entries.example: Choosing a city to move to: A/B/C × rent, commute, job market → B wins on rent and jobs; trade-off: longer winters.

entries.name: Pre-mortem
entries.when: before starting something that could fail
entries.form: 1) imagine it has failed 2) list the most likely reasons 3) fix or guard the top ones before starting.
entries.example: Database migration 'failed because the backup was never test-restored' → test-restore first.

entries.name: Hypothesis loop
entries.when: diagnosing, investigating, research with unknown cause
entries.form: observe → 2-3 hypotheses → pick the test that separates them → run it → update → repeat until one survives.
entries.example: Wi-Fi drops every evening: router, interference or provider? A wired test first separates the provider from the rest.

entries.name: Issue tree
entries.when: big or messy goals
entries.form: Split the goal into non-overlapping, complete branches; recurse to actionable leaves; solve leaves; recombine.
entries.example: Cut monthly costs → housing / transport / food / subscriptions → each to concrete actions.

entries.name: Plan-act-verify
entries.when: multi-step work with tools, files or code
entries.form: small step → act → verify against what you expected → revise; never chain two unverified risky steps.
entries.example: Reorganising a music library: move one album, check the player still finds it, then move the rest.

entries.name: Root-cause fix
entries.when: a recurring problem
entries.form: describe the failure → why ×5 → fix at the level that prevents recurrence → check nothing else depended on the old behaviour.
entries.example: Report wrong each month → manual copy step → automate the import, keep a check total.

entries.name: OODA loop
entries.when: fast-changing situations, interactive tasks, browsing
entries.form: observe → orient (what does it mean here?) → decide → act; re-loop quickly when things change.
entries.example: A site shows a sign-in wall: observe, orient (content gated), decide (other source), act.

entries.name: First-principles rebuild
entries.when: redesigning, or when the usual approach is bloated or failing
entries.form: list what is truly required → strip assumptions → build the minimal version → add back only what is justified.
entries.example: Backup system: requirement is 'restore any file from last week' → one versioned sync, not three tools.

entries.name: Compare and contrast
entries.when: two or more things, versions, sources or options
entries.form: same dimensions for each → similarities → differences → which difference matters for the purpose.
entries.example: Two insurance policies: premium, deductible, exclusions — for a renter who cycles, the exclusion list is the difference that matters.

entries.name: Argument map
entries.when: evaluating a claim, debate, or persuasive text
entries.form: claim → reasons → evidence for each → objections → rebuttals → net assessment with confidence.
entries.example: 'Remote work lowers productivity': study quality, selection effects, what is measured.

entries.name: Scenario branching
entries.when: planning under an uncertain future
entries.form: 2-4 plausible futures → best action in each → choose the action that holds up across them.
entries.example: Job offer: company grows / flat / shrinks → negotiate equity and severance, not only salary.

entries.name: Debugging
entries.when: code or a system misbehaves
entries.form: reproduce → isolate (bisect inputs or changes) → hypothesise → minimal fix → test → check side effects.
entries.example: A script fails on some inputs → reproduce with one → it has an unexpected encoding → handle it, rerun everything.

entries.name: Research funnel
entries.when: questions needing sources
entries.form: broad scan → identify authoritative sources → narrow to specifics → cross-check → synthesise with citations.
entries.example: Drug interaction: scan, then official label + a clinical reference, cross-check, cite both.

entries.name: Trade-off analysis
entries.when: no option dominates
entries.form: what each option gains and loses → who bears the costs → reversibility → recommendation with the stated trade-off.
entries.example: Faster model vs more accurate one: interactive chat favours speed; reports favour accuracy.

entries.name: Explanation ladder
entries.when: explaining or teaching
entries.form: one-line answer → key reasons → details → caveats, at the asker's level.
entries.example: Why the sky is blue: short wavelengths scatter more → Rayleigh scattering → why sunsets are red.

entries.name: Interests not positions
entries.when: conflicts, negotiations, messages to people
entries.form: interests behind each position → options for mutual gain → objective criteria → each side's walk-away alternative.
entries.example: Landlord wants +10%: interest is reliable income → offer a longer lease for +4%.

entries.name: Fermi estimate
entries.when: a number is needed and no source has it
entries.form: break into factors → estimate each with a range → combine → sanity-check the order of magnitude.
entries.example: Piano tuners in a city: households × pianos per household × tunings a year / tunings per tuner.

entries.name: Ethics check
entries.when: actions affecting other people, privacy, money or safety
entries.form: who is affected → consent → honesty → harms vs benefits → would this be fine if made public?
entries.example: Auto-replying to emails as the user: consent for each kind of message, never impersonate in new threads.
